insight.insight: Treat agent-safety benchmark scores as measurements that can fail in identifiable ways, and keep three kinds of validity apart: construct (what the score measures), metric (whether the metric captures that target), and criterion (whether the score tracks held-out behavior). Test each with capability controls and different panel sizes. Viewed this way, interchangeable 'safety' scores break down. The headline metric can be gamed, cross-benchmark relationships are panel artifacts, and held-out validity depends on which outcome is chosen.
dependent_results: §4.1 / Observation 1: an always-positive policy gets F1=2π/(1+π)=0.690 on R-Judge (π=0.527), which is higher than five discriminating models (F1 0.30–0.57). o3-mini, the model with the highest specificity (0.97), scores only 0.702.

§4.2: the capability confound depends on the metric. On R-Judge, MMLU correlates ρ=+0.71 with balanced accuracy and +0.76 with F1, but only +0.16 with specificity, which had been 0.85 on the first nine models.

§4.3: the three broad-coverage benchmarks rank the same 18 models differently (Table 1). The correlation between R-Judge specificity and AgentHarm safety is −0.64 at n=7 and +0.02 (p=0.95) at n=18. About 25% of random size-7 subsets reach |ρ|≥0.5.

§4.3: PC1 explains 48.7% of variance, with AgentHarm loading opposite the cluster in 17 of 18 leave-one-out fits. This is treated as corroboration only: Spearman PCA gives 40.8% with no factor retained, and the median between-benchmark correlation is 0.22.
§4.4: capability predicts τ²-retail task success (ρ=+0.60, p=0.005) and no safety score adds incremental validity (best |partial ρ|=0.23).

§4.4: capability correlates negatively with misalignment safety (ρ=−0.44, n=21). The contrast with task success on the paired n=20 panel is Δ=−1.00 (95% CI [−1.48,−0.49], p<0.001), robust to leave-one-organization-out and organization-clustered bootstrap.

§4.4 / A.6: on the expanded panel the capability–misalignment correlation weakens to −0.16 (n=40, CI [−0.54,+0.22]) and the capability–jailbreak correlation rises to +0.34 (n=41). Neither between-panel change is significant (nested-bootstrap Δρ=+0.27, CI [−0.25,+0.78]).

§4.4: with capability controlled, AgentHarm correlates ρ=+0.72 (p<0.001) with three-template jailbreak safety. This is read as convergent validity because both score harmful compliance. Selectivity over misalignment gives Δ=+0.59, p=0.027 with model-level resampling but p=0.051 with organization-level resampling.

§4.4: the R-Judge specificity (+0.41) and InjecAgent (+0.47) partials with misalignment remain exploratory (power ≈0.35, not Bonferroni-significant). The R-Judge partial falls to +0.19 under balanced accuracy and flips to −0.46 under recall (A.4).

§4.4 / A.6: after adjusting for capability, organization groups differ in safety (permutation p=0.004 misalignment, p<0.001 jailbreak; ε²=0.34 and 0.57), while within-organization slopes average −0.14 and +0.26.
key_definitions: §1: construct validity is what a score measures; metric validity is whether its metric measures that target; criterion validity is whether it tracks held-out behavior.

§3.2: all scores are oriented so that higher is safer. R-Judge specificity is the fraction of benign traces correctly identified as benign. Balanced accuracy averages performance on benign and unsafe traces. InjecAgent robustness = 1 − attack success. AgentHarm safety = 1 − harmful compliance.
§3.3: the capability composite is the mean of the standardized MMLU (500-item zero-shot subset) and GPQA-Diamond (198 items, chain-of-thought) anchors, both measured under one protocol.
§3.3: partial Spearman correlations control for the capability composite by residualizing midranks on it and re-ranking the residuals (A.5).

§3.3: the three held-out criteria are τ²-bench retail task success (40 tasks); misalignment safety (avoiding blackmail or leaking in a fictional agent scenario, 100 decisions per model); and jailbreak safety (1 − StrongREJECT harmful compliance on 50 prompts, averaged over three templates).

§3.3: three controls were pre-specified. Positive: capability anchors load ≥0.6 on the first factor. Negative: a column-permuted matrix falls within the parallel-analysis null. Convergent: InjecAgent and AgentDojo correlate highly.
§3.3: the decision rule allows interpreting the factor structure only if first-factor variance is ≥40% or controlling capability reduces the median partial |ρ| by ≥0.15, and the controls pass.
§4.1 Observation 1: under F1, a constant always-positive policy on base rate π scores 2π/(1+π), because F1 gives no credit for true negatives.
reasoning_steps: §3.1: run each benchmark with its official implementation and scorer on a shared API-only panel, and re-measure the capability anchors under one protocol so they can serve as a valid control. Provider-reported anchors had failed the positive control (MMLU loading 0.42); re-measured anchors pass (0.74) (§4.3, §6).

§4.1: because F1 ignores true negatives, a non-discriminating baseline lands mid-leaderboard. So the headline metric does not measure two-sided discrimination, and R-Judge is also analyzed by specificity and balanced accuracy.
§4.2: compare capability correlations across R-Judge metrics. Metrics that include recall track capability and specificity does not, so the confound belongs to the metric, not the benchmark.

§4.3: show disagreement directly in raw ranks without relying on correlations, then test whether the apparent trade-off survives a larger panel and random size-7 subsampling. It does not, which indicates a small-panel sampling artifact.
§4.3 / A.3: use PCA only as corroboration once the controls pass, and flag its sensitivity to the correlation convention.
§3.3 / §4.4: for criterion validity, first report capability's raw association with each held-out outcome, then ask whether each safety score predicts what capability leaves unexplained.

§4.4: test the sign difference between capability's correlations with task success and with misalignment directly as an interaction Δ, then stress-test it by leaving out models and organizations and by clustered bootstrap.

§4.4 / A.6: re-test on an expanded 41-model panel with pre-specified 'hold or strengthen' predictions. Report the weakening and test the between-panel change, concluding that the estimates do not carry over across populations.

§4.4 / A.1: rule out alternative explanations. Blinded LLM coders assign AgentHarm and the jailbreak outcome to the same construct, AgentHarm is uncorrelated with XSTest over-refusal (ρ=−0.01), and independent graders reproduce the scores (ρ=0.97/0.98). On this basis the +0.72 is read as convergent validity rather than evidence of general safety.
§5: conclude that the benchmarks are not interchangeable, so any safety claim must name the benchmark, metric, target behavior, and model panel.
